newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to give Brussels Cr Lyonnais plan this week.
newsitem.headline: France to give Brussels Cr Lyonnais plan this week.

text.p: France said on Tuesday it would submit a long-awaited plan to privatise struggling state bank Credit Lyonnais to the European Commission later this week.
"The rescue plan, the strategic plan will be transmitted to Brussels toward the end of the week," a finance ministry official said.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis gave the commitment to European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert at a meeting on Monday in Brussels, the official said.
She would not comment on newspaper reports the European Commission, which must approve any new state aid, expects the privatisation plan to cost some 30 billion francs ($5.2 billion).

"We will not know (the full cost) until we've started to put the plan into operation," she said. "Before that it is pure speculation." Credit Lyonnais, once France's flagship bank, is still suffering from an expansion spree which backfired and led to massive losses.

The fresh state aid would be on top of 45 billion francs from the taxpayer the bank received in 1995 and 3.9 billion in emergency help it got late last year to allow it to report a modest 1996 first half profit of 67 million francs.

Newspaper have reported that some 15-20 billion francs would be needed to scrap heavy financial penalties imposed on Credit Lyonnais in the 1995 state rescue plan. The remainder would be linked to the need to recapitalise the bank and improve its solvency ratios.
